page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 32.0 GB of system memory allocating 4.0 GB per core, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing the instance in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth operations fall within the average range, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 117.03 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 77.42 GB/sec. Database operations and web serving capabilities are stable, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 3794.54 and static web serving throughput of 8.45 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but show limitations on larger workloads, with prompt processing for a 7B model dropping to a weak 18.38 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provide reliable, non-burstable performance suitable for production environments without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage enhances its value for disk-I/O sensitive applications. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including medium-scale web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
